AST 36, ALT 32, alk phos 102. Mild congestive pattern.

raw_record.name: Christopher Anderson

WBC 11.2 with mild lymphocyte predominance. Hgb 13.4.

data_gathering.label: Characterise prior BP readings
data_gathering.evidence: Asks how many readings, where (pharmacy/home/clinic) and the actual values to confirm pattern of elevation rather than a single high reading.

data_gathering.label: Screen for end-organ symptoms
data_gathering.evidence: Asks specifically about target-organ symptoms — headaches, visual changes, chest pain, breathlessness, leg swelling, focal neurology — to exclude accelerated/complicated hypertension.

data_gathering.label: Family history of cardiovascular disease
data_gathering.evidence: Elicits family history of hypertension, premature CVD or stroke (case states both parents hypertensive).

data_gathering.label: Lifestyle risk assessment
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about salt intake, alcohol, exercise/sedentary behaviour, diet and smoking status (case: heavy salt use, sedentary).

data_gathering.label: Secondary-cause screen
data_gathering.evidence: Asks at least one question that screens for secondary hypertension — e.g. snoring/OSA, paroxysmal sweating/palpitations, recreational drug or NSAID/decongestant use, or known renal disease.

data_gathering.label: Explore ICE
data_gathering.evidence: Explores the patient's ideas, concerns and expectations — particularly his belief that he "feels fine" and any worry about needing tablets for life.

data_gathering.label: Cardiovascular risk factors
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about diabetes, cholesterol, prior CVD, weight/BMI to feed into a 10-year CVD risk estimate.

clinical_management.label: Confirm diagnosis with ABPM or HBPM
clinical_management.evidence: Explicitly arranges 24-hour ambulatory monitoring or home BP monitoring (≥135/85 daytime average) before labelling as hypertension, rather than diagnosing from clinic readings alone.

clinical_management.label: Offer lifestyle advice
clinical_management.evidence: Gives specific lifestyle advice — reduce salt (<6 g/day), Mediterranean-style diet, regular aerobic exercise, alcohol within limits, weight loss if applicable.

clinical_management.label: Discuss starting drug treatment
clinical_management.evidence: Recognises stage 1 hypertension with target-organ damage (LVH on ECG) in a patient under 80 and discusses starting antihypertensive medication, not lifestyle alone.

clinical_management.label: First-line drug choice
clinical_management.evidence: Selects an ACE inhibitor or ARB as step 1 (patient is under 55, not stated to be of Black African/Caribbean origin) — names a specific agent such as ramipril or losartan.

clinical_management.label: State the BP target
clinical_management.evidence: Explicitly states a clinic BP target below 140/90 mmHg for an adult under 80.

clinical_management.label: Plan investigations for end-organ damage and CVD risk
clinical_management.evidence: Orders or names the standard work-up: urine ACR, U&Es, HbA1c, lipid profile, fundoscopy, and notes the LVH already seen on ECG.

interpersonal.label: Open with agenda-setting
interpersonal.evidence: Greets the patient, introduces self, checks the reason for attendance and negotiates the agenda for the consultation.

interpersonal.label: Acknowledge "I feel fine"
interpersonal.evidence: Empathically addresses that the patient is asymptomatic — names hypertension as a "silent" condition and validates that it is reasonable to feel sceptical without being dismissive.

interpersonal.label: Jargon-free explanation
interpersonal.evidence: Explains hypertension, why it matters long-term, and what ABPM/HBPM involves in plain English without unexplained acronyms.

interpersonal.label: Shared decision making on medication
interpersonal.evidence: Presents lifestyle and pharmacological options, discusses pros/cons of starting a tablet now, and checks the patient's preference rather than instructing.

interpersonal.label: Summarise and check understanding
interpersonal.evidence: Summarises the plan at the end (monitoring, lifestyle, likely medication, follow-up) and invites questions or teach-back.

required_elements: Return urgently if severe headache, visual disturbance, chest pain, breathlessness or focal neurological symptoms develop
Seek same-day review if home readings are persistently 180/120 mmHg or higher
Agreed timeframe for ABPM/HBPM results review and follow-up appointment

data_gathering.label: Characterise polyuria and polydipsia
data_gathering.evidence: Quantifies onset, duration, nocturia frequency and volume of fluid intake to establish the osmotic-symptom pattern (case: ~2 months, frequent urination, constant thirst).

data_gathering.label: Quantify weight loss
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about intentional vs unintentional weight loss and quantifies it (case: 5 kg unintentional).

data_gathering.label: Screen for DKA / type 1 features
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, deep/rapid breathing, drowsiness or fruity breath to rule out DKA before deciding on outpatient management.

data_gathering.label: Complications screen
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about visual changes, foot numbness/tingling, erectile dysfunction, recurrent infections (case: blurry vision, recurrent yeast infections).

data_gathering.label: Family and cardiovascular risk history
data_gathering.evidence: Elicits family history of diabetes (case: mother and brother) plus smoking, hypertension, lipids and prior CVD as part of overall risk assessment.

data_gathering.label: Lifestyle and dietary baseline
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about typical diet, sugary drinks, physical activity and weight history to anchor later lifestyle advice.

data_gathering.label: Explore ICE
data_gathering.evidence: Explores ideas, concerns and expectations — what the patient thinks is wrong, fears about insulin/diabetes complications, and what she wants from today.

clinical_management.label: Confirm diagnosis biochemically
clinical_management.evidence: Recognises symptomatic hyperglycaemia with random glucose 286 mg/dL plus 3+ glucosuria as diagnostic of diabetes, and orders an HbA1c to characterise glycaemic burden.

clinical_management.label: Offer structured education
clinical_management.evidence: Explicitly refers or signposts to a structured patient education programme (e.g. DESMOND) at the time of diagnosis.

clinical_management.label: Dietary and lifestyle advice
clinical_management.evidence: Gives specific dietary advice — high-fibre/low-glycaemic-index carbohydrates, fruit/veg/wholegrains/pulses, oily fish, low saturated fat — plus weight management and physical activity.

clinical_management.label: Initiate first-line pharmacotherapy
clinical_management.evidence: Starts modified-release metformin together with an SGLT-2 inhibitor as first-line therapy, named explicitly (e.g. metformin MR + empagliflozin or dapagliflozin).

clinical_management.label: State HbA1c target
clinical_management.evidence: Names a target HbA1c — 48 mmol/mol (6.5%) on a non-hypoglycaemic regimen, or 53 mmol/mol (7.0%) if on a sulfonylurea/insulin later.

clinical_management.label: Plan HbA1c monitoring
clinical_management.evidence: Schedules HbA1c every 3–6 months until stable, then 6-monthly.

interpersonal.label: Introduce self and agenda
interpersonal.evidence: Greets the patient, introduces self and clarifies the reason for the visit before launching into questions.

interpersonal.label: Empathic delivery of new diagnosis
interpersonal.evidence: Names diabetes as a new diagnosis warmly, pauses, acknowledges feelings (uses Naming/Understanding/Respecting/Supporting/Exploring) before piling on management detail.

interpersonal.label: Jargon-free explanation
interpersonal.evidence: Explains type 2 diabetes, HbA1c, metformin and SGLT-2 inhibitor in plain English (e.g. "a tablet that helps your kidneys remove sugar in the urine") rather than acronym-heavy speech.

interpersonal.label: Shared decision on treatment
interpersonal.evidence: Discusses options, side-effect profile (GI upset with metformin, genital thrush/UTI with SGLT-2) and checks preferences before prescribing.

interpersonal.label: Summarise and chunk-and-check
interpersonal.evidence: Summarises the plan in chunks, checks understanding (teach-back) and offers written information.

required_elements: Seek urgent same-day care for vomiting, abdominal pain, drowsiness, deep/rapid breathing or inability to keep fluids down (DKA features)
Stop SGLT-2 inhibitor and seek review during acute illness, dehydration or before surgery (sick-day rules)
Agreed timeframe for HbA1c follow-up and structured-education enrolment

data_gathering.label: Characterise the cough and sputum
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about cough duration, productive vs dry, sputum colour and volume, and any haemoptysis (case: 5-day productive cough with yellow-green sputum).

data_gathering.label: Characterise pleuritic chest pain
data_gathering.evidence: Uses SOCRATES on the chest pain — site, radiation, relation to deep breath/cough, severity (case: sharp, right-sided, pleuritic).

data_gathering.label: Red-flag/severity symptoms
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about confusion, breathlessness at rest, dizziness, syncope, reduced urine output, and quantifies fever — features that would push severity stratification toward intermediate/high risk.

data_gathering.label: Comorbidity and risk-factor screen
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about COPD/asthma, diabetes, immunosuppression, recent hospital admission, smoking and alcohol — to flag at-risk groups and exclude HAP/aspiration.

data_gathering.label: Exposures and contacts
data_gathering.evidence: Asks about sick contacts, recent travel, occupation and pets/birds (case: colleague with similar illness; consider atypical/zoonotic exposure).

data_gathering.label: Vaccination and drug history
data_gathering.evidence: Checks influenza/COVID/pneumococcal vaccination status, regular medications and drug allergies (especially penicillin) before prescribing.

data_gathering.label: Explore ICE
data_gathering.evidence: Explores the patient's ideas, concerns and expectations — particularly fears about pneumonia or hospital admission and time off work.

clinical_management.label: Calculate CRB-65 in the community setting
clinical_management.evidence: Explicitly calculates CRB-65 (confusion, RR ≥30, BP <90/≤60, age ≥65) at this GP/polyclinic encounter — case scores 0, supporting low-risk community management.

clinical_management.label: Decide on community management
clinical_management.evidence: Documents that the patient is low risk on CRB-65 and suitable for oral antibiotics at home rather than IV/admission.

clinical_management.label: Start antibiotics promptly
clinical_management.evidence: States that antibiotics should be started as soon as the diagnosis is made (and within 4 hours if presenting to hospital) — does not defer pending sputum culture.

clinical_management.label: Choose an appropriate first-line oral regimen
clinical_management.evidence: Names a specific oral first-line agent appropriate for low-severity CAP (e.g. amoxicillin 500 mg TDS) and an alternative if penicillin-allergic (e.g. doxycycline or a macrolide).

clinical_management.label: Course duration
clinical_management.evidence: States 5 days of treatment, with extension only if microbiology suggests it or the patient is not clinically stable at review.

clinical_management.label: No routine follow-up CXR
clinical_management.evidence: Avoids ordering a routine follow-up chest X-ray; if mentioned, reserves it for persistent symptoms or higher-risk groups (e.g. smokers >50).

interpersonal.label: Open with agenda-setting
interpersonal.evidence: Greets the patient, introduces self and clarifies the reason for attendance.

interpersonal.label: Empathic acknowledgement
interpersonal.evidence: Acknowledges that 5 days of fever and pleuritic pain is unpleasant and likely worrying — names and validates the feeling rather than rushing to diagnostics.

interpersonal.label: Jargon-free explanation of diagnosis
interpersonal.evidence: Explains pneumonia, what the chest X-ray showed, why oral antibiotics are appropriate now and what to expect over the next 3–5 days, in plain English.

interpersonal.label: Shared decision and adherence check
interpersonal.evidence: Confirms the patient can take oral antibiotics, checks for allergies, asks about ability to rest at home and identifies a responsible adult if needed.

interpersonal.label: Summarise the plan
interpersonal.evidence: Summarises antibiotic, duration, expected course, follow-up and red flags at the end of the consultation.

required_elements: Return urgently or call 999 if breathlessness worsens, new confusion, chest pain at rest, lips/fingertips turn blue, or unable to keep fluids down
Seek review if symptoms have not started to improve within 3 days of starting antibiotics
Advice on common antibiotic side effects (GI upset, rash, candidiasis) and when to stop and seek help

references.title: Type 2 diabetes in adults: management (NG28)
